column6:
% of planned NIAT program activities, covering both curriculum slots and co-curricular activities like tech workshops, that were not scheduled and executed in actual delivery. Planned activity count is set during curriculum design. Actual delivery count is tracked by the onground Program Ops team. CSI team is accountable for driving this to zero through live session solutioning and execution support.

Formula: (Planned activities − Executed activities) / Planned activities × 100.

% of Academy curriculum units compliant with applicable regulatory and quality frameworks such as NHQRF and Woolf at time of audit. Parallel metric to NIAT University Curriculum Compliance Rate but scoped to Academy and driven by external framework requirements rather than university BOS.

Formula: (Framework-compliant units delivered / Total units delivered) × 100.
Recommended audit cadence: per framework submission cycle.

Average cost incurred per approved BOS across university partners. Includes CSI team payroll costs and non-payroll costs (travel, liaison activities) attributed to BOS approval work. Excludes content production costs.

Note: First-time approvals cost more than renewals. As you scale from 17 to 34 universities in 2026, track new approvals vs renewals separately to avoid skewing the average.

column6:
Average time taken by the CSI team to resolve or escalate issues raised by university partners or program teams. CSI handles first-pass solutioning before escalating to Content or Product teams. Measures speed of response, not volume. Complements Feedback Resolution Efficiency (which tracks SLA compliance) but is distinct — TAT is more relevant at the CSI layer where university escalations are unpredictable and speed matters more than SLA adherence.

Tracked per issue category and per university.

CSI is expected to leverage AI tools to drive this cost down over time. Submitted to relevant regulatory frameworks as part of compliance reporting.

Tracked monthly.
